source_findings.finding: getAllPyObjects returns a deduplicated std::set of borrowed live wrapper pointers under the recursive wrapper-map lock. The proposal adds one owned reference per unique pointer, then releases one per pointer.

SbkDeallocWrapperCommon unregisters a wrapper before weakref and Python callbacks. Under the candidate standard GIL, wrapper pointers obtained from the map are live until the non-callback increment loop has pinned them.

The wrapper set is declared before qScopeGuard, so the guard executes while its referenced set still exists. Set allocation precedes all pins; Py_INCREF and construction of the trivial captured-lambda guard introduce no partial-pin allocation path.

Original visitor validity/ownership checks, C++ destruction, GIL release around Qt cleanup, application deletion, and MakeQAppWrapper reset remain in their original order. Wrapper lifetime is extended only until those original steps finish.

Releasing one wrapper cannot prematurely release a different still-pinned wrapper. Existing users keep their own references after the extra pin is dropped; unreferenced invalid wrappers can then finalize.
source_findings.source: proposed pin/release loops and Object::destroy in upstream/basewrapper.cpp

source_findings.finding: Public QApplication.shutdown dispatches runCleanupFunctions. That function pops each cleanup before invoking it, so the nested public shutdown probe does not recursively call the same destroyQCoreApplication cleanup. Only one begin/original-returned/released sequence occurs per guarded cycle.

qScopeGuard destructor is noexcept and calls its lambda when leaving scope. Ordinary C++ unwind while holding the GIL balances the pins by construction; this was not exercised using the rebuilt patch. Python finalizer exceptions are unraisable and were exercised separately.
